text: The LORD said to Moses: Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and say to them: No priest shall make himself unclean for any of his people who dies,
except for his closest relatives — his mother, his father, his son, his daughter, his brother,
or his virgin sister, close to him, who has never had a husband; for her he may make himself unclean.

versions.text: or his unmarried sister who is near to him, since she has had no husband; for her he may make himself unclean.
versions.explanation: "Unmarried sister... since she has had no husband" is redundant, and "since" turns a descriptive clause into a causal one. The Hebrew simply describes her as a virgin sister close to him who has never belonged to a man.

text:
He shall not make himself unclean for relatives by marriage among his people, and so profane himself.[^1]

[^1]: The Hebrew of this verse is obscure; it may mean that a priest must not defile himself for kin related to him only through marriage.

versions.text: He shall not make himself unclean as a husband among his people, and so profane himself.
versions.explanation: The clause is notoriously difficult in Hebrew; "as a husband among his people" is opaque to a listener. A clearer rendering with a brief footnote acknowledging the uncertainty aids oral comprehension.

text: Priests shall not shave bald patches on their heads, or trim the edges of their beards, or cut gashes in their flesh.
They shall be holy to their God and shall not profane the name of their God, for they present the offerings by fire to the LORD, the food of their God; therefore they shall be holy.
A priest shall not marry a woman defiled by prostitution, nor one who has been dishonored, nor a woman divorced from her husband, for the priest is holy to his God.
You shall treat him as holy, for he offers the food of your God. He shall be holy to you, for I am holy — I, the LORD, who makes you holy.

versions.text: You shall treat him as holy, for he offers the food of your God. He shall be holy to you, because I, the LORD, who make you holy, am holy.
versions.explanation: The nested clause "I, the LORD, who make you holy, am holy" is hard to follow when read aloud; recasting it keeps the same meaning with better rhythm.

text: If a priest's daughter defiles herself by prostitution, she profanes her father; she shall be burned with fire.

The priest who is highest among his brothers, on whose head the anointing oil has been poured and who has been ordained to wear the sacred garments, shall not let his hair hang loose or tear his clothes.
He shall not go near any dead body; he shall not make himself unclean even for his father or his mother.
He shall not leave the sanctuary or profane the sanctuary of his God, for the consecration of the anointing oil of his God is upon him. I am the LORD.
He shall marry a woman who is a virgin.
A widow, a divorced woman, or one dishonored by prostitution — these he shall not marry. He shall take as his wife a virgin from his own people,
so that he does not profane his offspring among his people; for I am the LORD, who makes him holy.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
Say to Aaron: For all generations to come, none of your descendants who has a defect may come near to offer the food of his God.
No man with a defect may come near: no one blind or lame, disfigured or deformed;
no one with a crippled foot or a crippled hand;
no one hunchbacked or dwarfed, or with a defect in his eye, or with festering or running sores, or with damaged testicles.
No descendant of Aaron the priest who has a defect shall come forward to present the offerings by fire to the LORD. Since he has a defect, he shall not come forward to offer the food of his God.
He may eat the food of his God, both the most holy and the holy;
but he shall not go near the curtain or approach the altar, because he has a defect, so that he does not profane my sanctuaries; for I am the LORD, who makes them holy.
So Moses told this to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites.
